title: StorageServicePlugin warns "storage adapter swapped (LocalStorageAdapter → LocalStorageAdapter) … files may be unreachable" on every clean boot
body:
Newly visible after #4084 unblocked boot-phase logging. Every `os dev` / `os serve` boot of `examples/app-todo` prints:

```
WARN StorageServicePlugin: storage adapter swapped (LocalStorageAdapter → LocalStorageAdapter).
Existing files were NOT migrated and may be unreachable through the new adapter.
```

The adapter was swapped for **the same adapter class**, and the warning claims a data-reachability risk that did not occur. It fires on a clean boot where nothing changed.

## Mechanism

`packages/services/service-storage/src/storage-service-plugin.ts`:

- `applySettings()` reads the `storage` settings namespace and bails only when *every* value is empty:
  ```ts
  const hasAny = Object.values(values).some((v) => v !== undefined && v !== null && v !== '');
  if (!hasAny) return;
  const next = await this.buildAdapterFromValues(values);
  this.storage.swap(next);           // line 335 — unconditional
  ```
- `swap()` then invokes the `onSwap` callback registered at line 172, which warns unconditionally:
  ```ts
  const prevName = (prev as any)?.constructor?.name ?? 'unknown';
  const nextName = (next as any)?.constructor?.name ?? 'unknown';
  ctx.logger.warn(`StorageServicePlugin: storage adapter swapped (${prevName} → ${nextName}). ` +
    'Existing files were NOT migrated and may be unreachable through the new adapter.');
  ```

Once the settings service has persisted defaults for the `storage` namespace, `hasAny` is true on every subsequent boot, so a same-kind, same-config adapter is rebuilt and swapped in, and the warning fires — forever.

## Why it is worth fixing rather than ignoring

The warning is correct and valuable for a *real* adapter change (Local → S3), which is genuinely a data-reachability event. Crying wolf on every boot is how an operator learns to skim past it — and this one now sits in the boot-diagnostics block right where real warnings land.

## Suggested fix

Skip the swap when the rebuilt adapter is equivalent to the current one (same class **and** same resolved config), so `onSwap` only fires on an actual change. Comparing constructor names alone is not enough — Local→Local with a different `rootDir` *is* a real migration hazard and must still warn.
